title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Thompson
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and the internal templates employees should use. The objective is to provide a single source of truth for expected controls, approval flows, owners, and practical examples to reduce ambiguity and help teams stay compliant with security and finance requirements.

Scope

Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and contingent workers across Redwood Inference. Exceptions require documented approval from the owning function and People Ops or Finance as indicated per section.

Document structure
- Section-level owners are listed at the top of each section.
- Procedures include step-by-step numbered tasks and approval matrices.
- Where appropriate, minimal example commands, templates, and configuration snippets are provided.

1) Access and Permissions
Owner: Security & Compliance (policy governance) / eng-platform (execution patterns)

Purpose
- Ensure least-privilege access across cloud resources, internal apps, and developer tooling.
- Standardize on onboarding/offboarding workflows and periodic access reviews.

Key policies
- Account provisioning: All new employee accounts require an approved onboarding ticket from People Ops and manager verification. Default role is "employee-level" with no elevated privileges.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): Services must use RBAC groups mapped to job functions; avoid granting individual service accounts broad roles.
- MFA: Multi-factor authentication required for all SSO-protected systems and cloud console access.
- Elevated access (Admin/Owner): Temporary elevations must use Just-In-Time (JIT) workflow and be timeboxed to a maximum of 8 hours by default.

Onboarding checklist (example)
1. People Ops creates employee record and submits provisioning request via internal IT portal.
2. Manager completes role and required systems checklist.
3. Security verify baseline training status before granting access to sensitive systems (KMS, audit logs, production consoles).
4. Credentials and SSO links delivered to employee with required 2FA setup.

Offboarding checklist (example)
1. People Ops creates offboarding ticket on termination/resignation.
2. Revoke SSO session tokens, remove from RBAC groups, rotate shared credentials if necessary.
3. Submit cloud account and repo access revocation tasks to eng-platform.
4. Archive employee-owned artifacts to a company-controlled location.

Access review cadence and metrics
- Quarterly access review for production and sensitive systems, tracked by Security.
- KPI: 100% of flagged accounts reviewed within 30 days of quarterly review.

Approval matrix (text table)
| Action | Required approver(s) | Escalation |
| Grant elevated cloud role | Manager + Security approver | Head of Eng for requests >30 days |
| Service account creation | Service owner + eng-platform | Security for any wide-scope roles |
| External collaborator (contractor) | Manager + People Ops | Legal for high-sensitivity access |

2) Change Management
Owner: eng-platform / eng-sre

Goal
- Reduce risk to production systems by standardizing changes through a documented and audited change control process that scales with risk level.

Change categorization
- Standard changes: low-risk, pre-authorized configuration updates (e.g., config toggle, non-production infra tweaks). No CAB approval required but must be logged.
- Normal changes: require change request (CR) filed; review by on-call and service owner; scheduled during maintenance windows where appropriate.
- Emergency changes: immediate remediation required; must be logged and have post-facto review within 24 hours.

Change request process (normal change)
1. Create CR in change-tracker with impact, rollback plan, test plan, and owner.
2. Service owner reviews and assigns impact level (low/medium/high).
3. eng-platform schedules change during approved maintenance window; notify stakeholders.
4. Execute change, run smoke tests, and record outcome.
5. Close CR with notes and retrospective if incident occurred.

SLOs and timeboxes
- Normal CR review turnaround: 48 business hours.
- Emergency post-change review: within 24 hours.
- All high-impact changes require a pre-change runbook and two approvers.

Change logging requirements
- CRs must include: change description, owner, start/end time, rollback steps, and verification tests. Attach related monitoring dashboards and alert links.

3) Data Management
Owner: Security & Compliance / Product Data Governance

Principles
- Classify data into three categories: Public, Internal, Confidential.
- Apply controls based on data classification: encryption at rest and transit for Confidential, retention limits, and access restrictions.

Data classification summary
- Public: Documentation, marketing assets. No access controls required beyond public-facing controls.
- Internal: Non-sensitive operational data (internal docs, non-PHI telemetry). Accessible to employees by default.
- Confidential: Customer data, PII, audit logs, keys, contractual IP. Strictly controlled.

Storage and retention
- Confidential data must be stored in approved systems with server-side encryption and KMS-managed keys.
- Retention windows: default = 24 months for Internal; Confidential retention is per contract but default 36 months unless otherwise specified.
- Data deletion: Requests to delete must follow the Data Deletion Request template and be logged in the data-sops register.

Data handling and transfer
- Cross-border data transfers require review by Legal and Security for regulated data.
- Use company-approved S3 buckets, databases, and secret stores for production data. Avoid ad-hoc export to personal storage.

Data access request flow (example)
1. Submit request via data-access-request form with justification and access duration.
2. Data owner reviews and approves with scope and expiry.
3. Security provisions temporary access and logs activity.

Audit and monitoring
- Audit logging for data access to Confidential buckets and databases is mandatory.
- Monthly anomaly reports for unusual access patterns; Security to triage.

4) Procurement and Expenses
Owner: Finance & Legal / Procurement lead

Goals
- Ensure spend is vetted, budget-aligned, and compliant with vendor and legal requirements. Provide clear rules for expense reimbursements and corporate card usage.

Procurement thresholds and approvals (text table)
| Spend amount | Required approval | Purchasing process |
| <= $1,000 | Manager | Use expense report or card |
| $1,001 - $10,000 | Manager + Finance | Purchase order (PO) or card with pre-approval |
| > $10,000 | Director + Finance + Legal | PO required, vendor risk review |

Vendor onboarding checklist
1. Submit vendor request form with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement performs vendor risk assessment (security, financial stability, compliance).
3. Legal reviews and signs contract and data processing addenda (DPA) if needed.
4. Finance creates PO or approves card payment.

Expense reimbursement rules
- Employees should submit expenses within 30 days with receipts.
- Per diem for travel set by role and region (see Travel Policies).
- Company card misuse will be reviewed; repeated violations escalate to People Ops.

5) Vendor Management
Owner: Procurement / Security & Compliance

Purpose
- Manage vendor lifecycle from selection and risk assessment through contract renewal and offboarding. Ensure third-party compliance with security and data requirements.

Vendor risk tiers
- Low: non-critical SaaS with no access to sensitive data. Annual review.
- Medium: vendors with access to internal systems or aggregated customer data. Security questionnaire required and semi-annual review.
- High: vendors with access to customer PII or ability to execute code in our environment (e.g., CI/CD integration). Full security assessment, DPA, and quarterly review.

Vendor lifecycle steps
1. Request & justification (initiated by requester).
2. Procurement + Security complete risk evaluation.
3. Legal finalizes contract and DPA.
4. Onboarded to vendor registry with assigned owner and renewal date.
5. Periodic reviews and renewal approvals 60 days before contract end.

Termination and offboarding
- Remove vendor accounts and credentials, rotate any shared secrets, and archive related data per data retention rules.

6) Travel Policies
Owner: People Ops / Finance

Purpose
- Provide clear expectations for business travel booking, approvals, per diems, and expense reporting. Support safe travel practices and cost-effective choices.

Booking and approvals
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval. International travel additionally requires People Ops notification for safety and visa support.
- Preferred booking channels: company travel portal or approved travel agency. Use corporate rates where available.

Per diem and allowable expenses
- Per diem by region; employees may choose to expense actuals with receipts. See travel-per-diem template in Internal Templates.
- Allowable expenses include transportation, lodging (standard room), business meals, ground transport. Alcohol is allowed within reasonable limits if part of a business activity and must be itemized.

Safety and emergency procedures
- Register trip with People Ops for international travel.
- In case of emergency, contact People Ops emergency hotline and local consulate if required.

7) Internal Templates and Examples
Owner: People Ops / Finance / Legal

Templates available (use these canonical templates whenever applicable):
- Expense report template (expense-report-template.xlsx)
- Vendor request form (vendor-request-form.md)
- Data deletion request (data-deletion-request.md)
- Change Request template (change-request-template.md)
- Access request form (access-request-form.md)
- Travel per diem and approval form (travel-per-diem-template.pdf)

Template usage guidance
- Always attach a completed template to the originating ticket (Finance, Procurement, or Security).
- Populate required fields in full to avoid delays: cost center, justification, requested dates, requested approvers.

Governance and review
- This consolidated policy document will be reviewed annually by People Ops with input from Security, Finance, and Legal.
- Major changes to any section require cross-functional review and must be published with an edit summary indicating owners and the rationale.

Escalation paths
- Policy clarifications: People Ops (people-ops@redwoodai.com)
- Security incidents or suspected data leakage: security@redwoodai.com and PagerDuty incident channel.
- Procurement disputes or contract issues: procurement@redwoodai.com or legal@redwoodai.com.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Quick commands and example snippets
  - Example: Rotate service account key (kubernetes secret rotation)
    1. kubectl -n platform get secret my-service-account -o yaml > secret.yaml
    2. Update key material and apply: kubectl apply -f secret.yaml
    3. Notify eng-platform and run smoke tests.

- Appendix B: Contact matrix
  - People Ops: people-ops@redwoodai.com
  - Security: security@redwoodai.com
  - Procurement: procurement@redwoodai.com
  - Finance: finance@redwoodai.com
